learning_objective: The learner will classify eight replies to a teammate's statement as paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling, advice, or judgment, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** listening-responses
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify eight replies to a teammate's statement as paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling, advice, or judgment, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/health-education/tree/main/docs/sims/active-listening-checklist-microsim
**Prerequisites:** active listening and its parts (paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling), advice, judgment (all defined in the section "Communication, Listening, and Conflict" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner places each of 8 replies in one of five bins and submits it. A placement is correct when it matches the "Correct kind" column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Giving advice is a way of listening. (2) Agreeing with someone is the same as understanding them. (3) A question is always a clarifying question. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying replies by what they do, not by their tone, shows the learner that kind and well-meant replies may still be advice or judgment. Pairs of replies about the same statement make the distinction concrete. **Content:** The statement every reply answers: a teammate says, "I'm not going to present. I always mess it up in front of people." Five bins with definitions: | Kind | Definition shown | |---|---| | Paraphrase | Restates what the speaker said in your own words | | Clarifying question | Asks the speaker to say more about what they mean | | Reflecting feeling | Names the feeling the speaker seems to have | | Advice | Tells the speaker what to do | | Judgment | Evaluates or argues with what the speaker said | Eight replies: | # | Reply shown to the learner | Correct kind | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | "So you're worried you'll make a mistake in front of the class." | Paraphrase | It restates what the teammate said. | | 2 | "Just practice more and you'll be fine." | Advice | It tells the teammate what to do. | | 3 | "What happens when you feel like you mess it up?" | Clarifying question | It asks the teammate to say more. | | 4 | "You always say that, and it's never as bad as you think." | Judgment | It argues with the teammate's view. | | 5 | "It sounds like you're nervous about being watched." | Reflecting feeling | It names the feeling behind the words. | | 6 | "You should write out what you want to say." | Advice | It tells the teammate what to do. | | 7 | "Can you tell me about a time that went badly?" | Clarifying question | It invites the teammate to explain more. | | 8 | "That's silly; everyone has to present." | Judgment | It dismisses the teammate's concern. | **Provenance:** The kinds follow the chapter section "Communication, Listening, and Conflict." The statement and replies are illustrative, written for this chapter. **Rules:** Each reply has exactly one correct kind, given in Content. A reply is scored on its first submitted placement only. The score counts first-attempt correct placements out of 8. Mastery is a score >= 7. The three active-listening kinds are paraphrase, clarifying question, and reflecting feeling. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the teammate's statement and one reply at a time, with the five kinds. 2. The learner places the reply and submits it. The sim marks it correct or incorrect and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may place it again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct kind and reason are shown. 4. After all 8 replies, the sim shows the score and states how many replies were active listening. 5. The learner should notice that three kinds are active listening and two are not, and that a kind-sounding reply can still be advice. **Feedback:** 8 replies, shuffled once per session, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: [kind]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the kind]." After the second attempt the correct kind is revealed and the reply counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 8" is shown. Final message for a score >= 7: "You can tell listening from advice and judgment." For a score < 7: "Review the five kinds and try again; the replies will be reshuffled." **Starting State:** The teammate's statement and reply 1 of the shuffled order are shown with the five kinds, the score "First-try correct: 0 of 8," and the prompt "What kind of reply is this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists the parts of active listening as paraphrase, clarifying question, and reflecting feeling, and names advice and judgment as the two common replies that are not. The mastery bar is 7 of 8.
